summary: Develop a practical MEAL strategy with indicators, data quality tools, feedback systems, and learning plans. Enrol in the five-day course.
lede: A MEAL strategy connects programme results frameworks with practical monitoring, accountability, evaluation and learning processes. Designed for MEAL officers, programme managers, evaluation specialists and accountability leads, this training helps teams build an evidence-to-action approach for programme decisions. You’ll practise defining indicators and baselines, assessing data quality, and designing feedback and learning processes that support reporting and programme adaptation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who coordinate, implement, analyse, or govern monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning activities across development and humanitarian programmes.
audience: Programme Managers using evidence to adapt implementation
Country or Portfolio Directors using MEAL dashboards
prerequisites: You should have practical experience supporting or managing a programme, project, monitoring activity, evaluation assignment, accountability process, or grant reporting cycle. Familiarity with logical frameworks, results-based management, or routine programme data is helpful. No coding is required. Advanced evaluation designs and AI-assisted analysis are covered at conceptual and operational application level, while MEAL strategy design, indicator planning, data quality tools, and reporting workflows receive hands-on practice.
